liam (sales): FYI — Velora Health signed a 12mo commit. They require HIPAA controls + 24/7 availability. Need presales runbook for capacity + security questionnaire answers. @nina can you own the POC handshake?

nina (solutions): On it. POC window 2 weeks, then production rollout. Can you share expected traffic mix (chat vs embeddings), p95 latency target, and whether they accept spot-backed burst?

liam (sales): Early asks: p95 latency target = 300ms for chat. Peak traffic: ~3k requests/minute (mix: 75% chat gen, 25% embeddings). Average chat output ~120 tokens; embedding is 1536-d float32. They want AZ spread and minimal risk from spot eviction. Prefer VPC with customer KMS.

arjun (infra): Quick Q: are those 3k RPS or RPM? Also what's average input length? I need tokens/sec to estimate KV cache and GPU sizing.

liam (sales): sorry — 3k/min (50 RPS). Average prompt ~40 tokens, response ~120 tokens => ~170 tokens per request on average. So ~8.5k tokens/sec sustained at peak.

arjun (infra): math check: 50 req/s * 170 tok = 8500 tok/s. On an A100-like instance with our inference stack, rough throughput ~130k tokens/s per GPU (int8 quantized, short seqs) — but with long context and chat concurrency overhead, plan for ~20-25% headroom. My preliminary sizing: reserve 2 GPUs for steady-state + 1 reserved hot pool for burst, and an autoscale group that can add up to 4 additional GPUs for sustained spikes. That gets us to ~7 GPUs peak (2 reserved + 1 hot + 4 autoscale).

maya (security): For HIPAA we need: VPC peering, CMEK (customer-managed keys), audit log retention policy (export to their SIEM), and SOC2 + BAA in place. POC must not touch PHI—use synthetic data. We'll answer questionnaire but need org contacts for encryption and legal.

nina (solutions): Noted. I'll provide a draft POC plan and questionnaire answers. Arjun, can you paste a sample autoscale policy we recommend? Also include AZ spread + eviction preference.

arjun (infra): Sample autoscale snippet below (POC suggestion):

```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_reserved_instances: 2
  max_instances: 8
  burst_pool: 1  # prewarmed reserved for low-latency spikes
  scale_metric: token_utilization_pct
  scale_up_threshold: 65
  scale_down_threshold: 30
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  az_spread: true
  spot_eviction_strategy: "prefer_spot_for_burst, fallback_to_on_demand"
  prewarm_on_deploy: true
```

arjun (infra): Notes: - Set token_utilization_pct based on 95th percentile tokens/sec from the POC. - Burst pool uses on-demand reserve to avoid cold start. - For Velora we recommend on-demand for reserved capacity (sustained) and spot for ephemeral autoscale if they accept eviction risk.

liam (sales): Cost sensitivity: customer wants predictable commit billing; they'd rather pay for reserved capacity + small burst credits. They view spot eviction as acceptable only for non-critical background embedding jobs.

maya (security): Affirmative on POC: we must ensure all encryption-at-rest keys are customer provisioned and that KMS audit logs are forwarded. Also need diagram for network isolation (DMZ, public endpoints via our edge + private peering).

nina (solutions): Action items: 1) Arjun to create two capacity options (A: 2 reserved + 1 hot + autoscale to 8; B: 4 reserved, no spot, autoscale to 6) with cost delta. 2) Maya to draft security questionnaire answers and network diagram. 3) Liam to coordinate Velora legal for BAA + KMS contacts. 4) I'll run a 2-day synthetic load test during POC to validate tokens/sec and p95.

deploy-bot: POC workspace "velora-health-poc-3467890123" created. Invite links: https://redwood.example/poc/velora-health-poc-3467890123

liam (sales): Thanks — Nina/Arjun/Maya, please sync tomorrow EOD with the short report. @nina please cc engineering stakeholders in the doc. :white_check_mark:
